note: Every approved look reference of Brix Town, in one list (ADR-0061). Files live in Art/Reference/<Category>/ and are named <Category><Subject>[_<Variant>].<ext> in PascalCase, so a name says what it is. 'locks' is what the reference decides; 'decision' the ADR and the owner's approval; 'made_by' the script that renders it; 'models' what the game is built from or measured against with it; 'status' proposed when it waits for the owner's approval; 'issues' what is seen wrong in it and not mended, for the owner to judge; 'was' the old names. 'places' says which reference each kind of place in the game is judged against, and which places have none: python Tools/reference_catalog.py --for <tour stop, lot id or place> answers it; a place's 'camera' names the tour stops that look through its reference's own camera (Tools/unreal/look_match.py compares those square by square). 'gaps' are references a category still lacks. Tools/reference_catalog.py checks this file against the folders and writes Art/Reference/index.html; run it after any change here.

references.title: The old-town alley at every hour and in every weather
references.locks: The look of the world (the old-town alley of style test 02: matte mottled plaster and stone, soft rounded forms, W1-W8) at morning, midday and dusk; at night with the lamps on, and with them off under a full and a new moon; and by day in cloud, rain, fog and snow. No haze at midday. Rain and snow fall, puddles lie with rings where the drops fall into them, and the snow lies, only where the sky is open over them: never under the passage's roof. Only the light and the weather change between them. Rain as the game's (Game/README Weather): thin pale streaks (4.5 mm), the open paving darker with a faint sheen in half-metre cells, soft-edged dark puddles with a little mirror and faint grey rings; none under a roof or arch.
references.decision: the owner, 2026-11-26: "approved" (a reference shows every setting, not one; replaces WorldLook and the alley of WorldHours; ADR-0061); its rain redone as the game's (the owner, 2026-11-26: "Yes, both"; drops half as wide); snow as small round balls, the near ones up to 30% smaller (the owner, 2026-11-26)

issues: The cream banners across the alley catch the gate lamp at dusk and at night and read as bright blocks.
People are lit like everything else: nobody stands out under a lamp at night.

references.title: The sky and its clouds at every hour and in every weather
references.locks: The sky over the town, seen from Market Square over the roofs: blue overhead fading to the pale haze at the horizon by day, warm towards the low sun at dusk, the night's dark blue with the town's glow low down; clouds as soft heaps on one layer about 1.2 km up, flat underneath and rounded on top, lit on the sun's side and shaded underneath, pink at dusk, lit from below by the town's lamps at night; how much of the sky they cover follows the weather (clear 0.36, cloudy 0.62, rain 0.97, fog 0.55, snow 0.92); at night the stars, the Milky Way and the full moon's disc. No planet (ADR-0064).

references.title: The light fittings as objects, in the four style lines
references.locks: Every light fitting of World/rules/lights.json as an object, laid out as the furniture lines are (the owner, 2026-11-26, with the picture of FurnitureLines: "i wanted this kind of reference"; "some thing that can be transported easily into unreal"): each a piece made as the furniture kits' pieces are, in Plain, Old Town, Workshop and Curve, standing in daylight with a person for scale. Three sheets, 27 fittings. Standing (on a floor or a table): floor lamp, arc floor lamp, table lamp, desk lamp, table lantern, candles, candelabra. Hung (on a wall or a ceiling): wall light, wall lantern, string lights, pendant, chandelier, ceiling light, ceiling panel, track spots, neon ring, and neon tubes in blue, green, red and amber. Street (the street's and the shops'; the owner: "may be we should not leave out street lamps or shop fittings. only mall fitting can be left out"): street lamp, square lamp, a wall lantern for a house wall, bollard light, a shop's sign and its lamp, shop pendant, shelf light. The home fittings are for the buying catalogue (the owner: "can you add more of these lights. all of these will be made available in buying catalog"). How each lights a room, its colour and the way its light falls, is on the room pictures (OrnamentsLight<Fitting>) and the colour sheet (Indoor, IndoorLightKinds).

references.decision: ADR-0065, ADR-0067; the owner, 2026-11-26: "i wanted this kind of reference"

Game/Content/Furniture (not exported yet: the fittings wait for this reference's approval, ADR-0066)
issues: The pieces of wall and the posts with an arm that the hung fittings are shown on are props of the sheet, not part of any piece; on the hung sheet they are bigger than the fittings.
Small fittings are hard to read at this distance (table lamps, candles, track spots); the standing sheet has much empty ground.
On the street sheet the tall lamps stand close: rows overlap and the square lamps' crossbars run into their neighbours; the Plain row is pale against the ground.
Daylight barely shows the colours of the lights; they are judged at night (IndoorLightKinds).
The neon tubes are the same in all four lines.
The table lamp stands on the ground with no table.

The wall light, ceiling light, neon tubes and every fitting added on 2026-11-26 (arc floor lamp, table lantern, wall lantern, chandelier, track spots, string lights, candelabra, neon ring, ceiling panel, and all seven of the street's and shops') are new designs made for this reference; none was an approved piece. The town's scripts lit the street with a plain lit box on a post, and the game's streets use one street lamp: which line it takes is the owner's to pick.

The first thirteen fittings are shown lighting the whole home room, the sixteen newer ones a plain corner: the two groups are not shown the same way. Every strength and price is an [ASSUMPTION]. Not in furnishing.json or the buying catalogue yet, and nothing exported to Unreal.

references.title: A home's room (the living room) at every hour
references.locks: The living of furniture_kit_18, closed on four sides with one window. In the world's light (the owner, 2026-11-26: "use the same color etc from world lighting"): by day only the sun and sky of the hour, through the window, with the sunlit street outside throwing its light in; lamps and the fire out by day; the boards a greyer wood, so the bounced light is not orange; at night the lamps a warm white (until the kinds of light, FURN-066), the fire lit, the full moon a cool patch through the window, a new moon only the window's starlight. No weather settings indoors (the owner). The wall facing the people throws light back onto them (the owner, 2026-11-26: "the wall opposite to the character is not reflecting light back"): by day a little of the day through the window, at night a share of the lamps' light in their colour. Every fire, in every reference, one red (the owner, 2026-11-26: "oven flame should be same color in all references and more red"): its flames glow red and catch no light; with no other light in a room its red takes the room over, as it should (the owner). Two more nights with the fire out as well as the lamps (the owner: "we need reference of moon lights when the fire place is turned off"): the full moon only through the window, dim and cool, a new moon very dark.

references.title: The kinds of light and their named colours, in a home's room at night
references.locks: The named colours of light of World/rules/lights.json and the fittings that share them (the owner, 2026-11-26: "when the room is lit by lights then the color should be decided by the light types"; "each colored light should have a name for different styles of lamps, lights, street lights etc. can share the color behavior"). Ten colours: Lantern amber (the palette's Lantern, for street lamps and lanterns to share), Warm white, Soft white, Neutral white, Cool white, Fire red, Neon blue, Neon green, Neon red, Neon amber (the owner: "we also need some cooler and even neon blue and green lights"; "add those 3 suggestions"). Thirteen fittings, each lit alone in the approved home room (IndoorHomeRoom) on a night with no moon and the fire out: floor lamp, table lamp, wall light and pendant in Warm white, desk lamp in Soft white, ceiling light in Neutral white, cool ceiling light in Cool white, wall lantern in Lantern amber, candles in Fire red (every fire one red, candles too: the owner, "Fire red"). Neon is an accent (the owner: "Weaker neon"): a tube of 8 to 10 W, shown with the room's own floor lamp, table lamp and fire lit, so the room keeps its colours and the tube tints its corner. A fitting's strength is its own; its colour is its named colour's. The sheet shows each fitting twice: at one exposure for all (the lamp-lit night's), and with the eye set for that light, at most 2.5 stops either way; each fitting has its own entry under Ornaments (OrnamentsLight<Fitting>), with the second picture.

references.decision: ADR-0065, ADR-0067; the owner, 2026-11-26, of the colours and fittings on a trial sheet: "Yes, propose it"

issues: Night only: dusk and the day hours are not shown for these lights.
Neon blue, green and red are saturated colours, against the palette rule W4 (muted and warm); allowed as weak accents by the owner's words (ADR-0067).
Neon amber is hard to tell from the fire-lit room it is shown in; neon red reads pink and tints more of the room than the other tubes at the same strength.
The pendant and both ceiling lights burn out at the shared exposure and flatten the room (little shade under the furniture); with the eye set for them they are not burnt but still flat.
Floor lamp, table lamp and desk lamp look alike: Soft white is barely different from Warm white.
Candles at the shared exposure are almost black; with the eye opened the room goes orange-red. They are lit at 3 W, as the hour script lights every fire, where the file says 6 W.
The room holds every fitting at once, so its walls are crowded with unlit tubes and wall fittings; the floor lamp and the desk lamp stand behind the person.
The wall light, the wall lantern, the ceiling lights and the neon tubes are simple fittings made for this reference; the furniture kits have none, and they are not approved pieces.

Every colour value and strength is an [ASSUMPTION] in lights.json until this is approved. Tried and dropped: neon tubes of 30 to 40 W alone in the room (the whole room one colour, as a filter); candles in a colour of their own (1.0, 0.60, 0.28).

references.title: Eastgate Mall's Great Court at every hour
references.locks: The shapes are the game's: the court as the mall's plan draws it (World/city_01/blocks/b_16_5.json; Tools/worldgen/mall_inside_01.py, ADR-0038): 92 x 192 m, three floors 6 m apart, the galleries' openings swelling round each atrium and pinching between them, bridges at the pinches, five round roof lights, the moving stairs, fountains, gardens, benches, planters and every outlet's front. The look is its own, from the owner's screenshots of the game's court (Art/StyleTests/mall_wanted_51/) taken further (the owner, 2026-11-26: "feel inspired and take a creative take on the look and feel add ornaments if required use glass and other material"): warm timber slats under the galleries, cream edges with a line of light along each and brass trim, glass balustrades with brass rails, slender cream columns with brass collars, plants hanging over the balustrades; a uniform polished stone floor of large tiles with hidden joints (the owner: "smoother and shiny", "hide the tile edges"), a brass inlay tracing the galleries' curves; the roof lights lightly tinted with a diamond lattice, a chandelier of globes and translucent banners hanging in each; grass islands in white kerbs with trees and flowers; moving stairs with dark treads, glass sides and brass rails; shop fronts with their signs in coloured glass, lit (MallsEastgateShop, ADR-0071). In the world's light: by day the sun and sky through the roof lights, the hidden lights under the edges low; at dusk and at night those at full in the hall lantern's warm white. No moonlit nights, no weather.

references.decision: the owner, 2026-11-26: "there will be more reference for mall required for screenshot in attached pics"; "use the shapes from the game for the mall interiors but texture, color, styling etc, please come up with your self"; "Approve it"; ADR-0038, ADR-0061, ADR-0066; made again with the glass shop signs, the owner, 2026-11-28: "Yes, every shop", "Approve, all four" (ADR-0071)

references.title: Eastgate Mall's south entrance from the forecourt, at every hour
references.locks: The shapes are the game's (Art/StyleTests/unreal_mall_entrance_55/): the shell's ribbon wall 14 m out from the hall (World/city_01/blocks/b_16_5.json shell, Tools/worldgen/mall_shell_01.py, ADR-0037), lifted over the south door into an arch 44 m wide and 12.5 m high, the porch's vault behind it with three lanterns hanging in it; the hall's curved doorway, 16 m wide, straight sides rising into a wide curve, glazed to the curve with thin brass mullions and a line of light round its edge; the concourse and its outlets seen through it, their fronts in the game's style (clear glass, thin dark mullions, a sign band in the kind's colour with its name); the forecourt's trees where the block puts them. The ribbon wall is one even honed cream stone with a soft satin sheen, no patches and no alternating tones (the owner, 2026-11-27: "alternate bands on the external structure is not looking good", "we shouldn't have patches. Malls are posh"); the slice's pattern kept: each ribbon laps a little over the one below over a thin dark groove. From dusk ground floodlights set in the forecourt 12 m out throw warm fans up the wall, six along it and two lighting the arch's crown (the owner: "place flood light on the ground away from the mall casting light on the dome"; lights.json ground_flood). In the world's light; no moonlit nights, no weather.

references.title: Eastgate Mall's Food Market egg hall as a food court, at every hour
references.locks: The shapes are the game's (Art/StyleTests/unreal_egg_hall_56/): the Food Market's round hall under the south-west egg (World/city_01/blocks/b_16_5.json halls[0], WLD-059, ADR-0038), 22 m in radius and three floors high, its drum walls, the walk in from the court ending in a balcony on each upper floor, the roof open over it in a round eye, the egg above (38 x 31 x 45 m, its middle 11 m up) a lattice of diamond openings onto the sky, six produce stalls where its staff stand, a tree in a round planter in the middle, lanterns hanging in a ring. Added (the owner, 2026-11-27, ADR-0070): food outlets skirting the drum on the ground floor, each an open counter between stone piers with its sign in its colour and its name backlit, lit menu boards and a kitchen behind; long tables for ten in a ring and round tables for four between them and near the tree. The look is the court's (ADR-0069) taken warmer: honed stone drums with a line of light round each floor and timber fins round the upper drum, polished stone floor with warm caramel and dark bands and brass rings let into it, the lattice in gold, timber and cream stalls under striped canopies, timber and brass seating; uplit piers, warm kitchens, opal pendants over the long tables. In the world's light: by day the sky and sun through the egg, the lanterns low; at dusk and night the egg dark and the lamps at full. No moonlit nights, no weather. The outlets' signs are coloured glass with backlit names (ADR-0071), not raked, as they follow the drum.

Food stall at skirting the wall are really nice and matches my vision but currently the colors and light is a bit bland and missing depth"; "Approve it"; ADR-0038, ADR-0066, ADR-0069, ADR-0070; made again with the glass shop signs, the owner, 2026-11-28: "Yes, every shop", "Approve, all four" (ADR-0071)

references.title: One of Eastgate Mall's shops close by, its glass sign, at every hour
references.locks: Every outlet's sign in Eastgate Mall, shown on The Linen Press on the south concourse (World/city_01/blocks/b_16_5.json, unit b_16_5_u15): a band over the front in its kind's colour (MALL_LOOK["signs"], the mall's own colours), even, behind a pane of clear glass, raked back 5 degrees so the glass shows the hall's lit ceiling as a thin line along its top; brass trim above and below it and a line of light under it; its name in cream letters lit from behind, on all day; a brass trough on three arms out from the galleries' slats above, its light (the sign lamp's kind, World/rules/lights.json) falling onto the sign all day. Below it the outlet's glass front between dark mullions, its inside lit, as the court's (MallsEastgateCourt). In the world's light: the sign looks the same at every hour; the hall round it follows the court. No moonlit nights, no weather.
